Essay Original:
In the future, nobody will buy printed newspapers or books because they will be able to read everything they want online without paying. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
With technology development, online reading has become increasingly popular, leading to the belief that printed newspapers and books will disappear as the free content is easy to access. While it is true that online platforms offer great convenience, I partly disagree with this idea because printed materials still provide unique value that cannot be fully replaced.
On the one hand, online reading brings about some good points that attract many readers.  First, they no longer need to go to the bookstores or libraries, as a lot of books, articles, and new stories are available on smartphones or computers. This is helpful for people who live in remote areas or have busy schedules. Another small advantage is the ability to access a wide variety of content of different languages or from different cultures. For example, someone in Vietnam can easily read American newspapers or a Japanese comic book through the internet. 
On the other hand, the advantages of online reading are significantly outweighed by the enduring appeal of physical books and newspapers. Most importantly, printed materials offer a superior reading experience and are gentler on the eyes compared to digital formats. Screen fatigue and exposure to blue light  make digital reading uncomfortable during long sessions, while paper-based reading remains physically comfortable and eye-friendly. Moreover, printed media enables better focus and concentration without getting distracted constantly by notifications and advertisements interrupt reading environment. The quiet and focused space not only makes reading more enjoyable but also promotes deeper comprehension and better retention of information. These advantages explain why paper books and newspapers will still exist and be bought in the future.
In conclusion, although digital reading offers great convenience and is often free of charge, I do not believe that printed books and newspapers will completely vanish. They still provide unique benefits in terms of reading comfort, educational use, and content quality. In the future, both forms are likely to coexist, serving different purposes and reader preferences.

With technology development, online reading has become increasingly popular, leading to the belief that printed newspapers and books will disappear as the free content is easy to access. While it is true that online platforms offer great convenience, I partly disagree with this idea because printed materials still provide unique value that cannot be fully replaced.
On the one hand, online reading brings about some good points that attract many readers.  First, they no longer need to go to the bookstores or libraries, as a lot of books, articles, and new stories are available on smartphones or computers. This is helpful for people who live in remote areas or have busy schedules. Another small advantage is the ability to access a wide variety of content of different languages or from different cultures. For example, someone in Vietnam can easily read American newspapers or a Japanese comic book through the internet. 
On the other hand, the advantages of online reading are significantly outweighed by the enduring appeal of physical books and newspapers. Most importantly, printed materials offer a superior reading experience and are gentler on the eyes compared to digital formats. Screen fatigue and exposure to blue light  make digital reading uncomfortable during long sessions, while paper-based reading remains physically comfortable and eye-friendly. Moreover, printed media enables better focus and concentration without getting distracted constantly by notifications and advertisements interrupt reading environment. The quiet and focused space not only makes reading more enjoyable but also promotes deeper comprehension and better retention of information. These advantages explain why paper books and newspapers will still exist and be bought in the future.
In conclusion, although digital reading offers great convenience and is often free of charge, I do not believe that printed books and newspapers will completely vanish. They still provide unique benefits in terms of reading comfort, educational use, and content quality. In the future, both forms are likely to coexist, serving different purposes and reader preferences.

There is an ongoing debate about whether public authorities should allocate their funds for exploring new existence in other plants or solving global issues. Although both schools of thought hold merit, my personal opinion expresses a strong alignment with the latter perspective. 
	Granted, advocates of the view that spend public money to discover other plants for new life based on remaining global problems. To avoid this circumstance, governments use their money to explore new existence in the universe. However, this line of reasoning presents certain limitations that it marginally brings a successful result despite long-term study. As a result, space science has been gradually developing that it may take a long time, even several decades to achieve a breakthrough in existing findings. Therefore, it sheds light on the drawbacks of this view.
	On the other hand, I believe that solving international issues by using public money is significantly essential. Firstly, instead of finding new life, the government should allocate money for manufacturing environmentally-friendly products, allowing the environmental problems to be improved radically. For example, replacing gasoline-fueled cars with zero-emission vehicles declines remarkably CO2 emissions. Secondly, investing in public infrastructures elevates the living standard and also maintains social stability. For instance, if medical facilities were enhanced with more modern equipments, the rate of disease would decrease noticeably. 
        In conclusion, while using public funds for finding other existence in the universe, I believe that it should be allocated for solving remaining global issues by improving environmental problems and infrastructure investments.

Task 2: While some people claim that advertising drives economic growth, others suggest it harms society by making individuals feel unhappy with themselves and their belongings. Discuss both views and give your opinion. 
Some people believe that advertising stimulates economic growth, while others argue that it undermines society by making people feel dissatisfied with what they have. This essay will discuss both perspectives and explain why I agree with the former viewpoint.
On the one hand, there are several reasons why people say advertising makes individuals feel bad about themselves and their belongings. Firstly, advertisements usually hype up about striking features and technologies on the latest gadgets and belittle the older ones. This can make an average person feel like they are not good enough unless they purchase the advertised products. To be more specific, fashion brands often invite influencers, or well-known figures to be their brand ambassadors for their advertisements, showing these people with expensive clothes, making watchers think that their wardrobes are stuck in the past, eventually leading to low self-esteem. Furthermore, this feeling can encourage people to spend their money wastefully for things that they may not actually need, making them become financial burdens for their families and lowering their overall living standards.
On the other hand, others, including myself, believe that advertising plays a significant role in driving economic growth. When companies advertise their products, people may be attracted and might want to buy more. The more money people spend, the more companies make profits. These returns can be used to create more job opportunities, build larger factories and create more inventions. Eventually, this cycle of spending and reinvestment is repeated and boosts the overall economy. Moreover, advertising informs people about new useful products, such as medicine or cutting-edge technologies, which potentially improve people’s quality of life. 

In conclusion, although some advertisements may promote unrealistic ideals, it is important to recognize that advertisements also inform people about the valuable products and services, which can improve their lives. Ultimately, when people consume more, it stimulates economic growth by making consumers to spend more.

While this notion has some validity, it is equally important to acknowledge that humans not only can act but also must take action to prevent the disappearance of endangered animals.

However, this reasoning fails to reflect the reality of the modern world, where the majority of endangered species are threatened directly by human activity. Practices such as deforestation, overhunting, and industrial pollution have accelerated extinction rates to unprecedented levels. In this situation, humans bear both a moral obligation and a practical responsibility to safeguard biodiversity. A vivid example is the case of tigers and elephants who are on the brink of extinction mainly due to poaching and habitat destruction. Therefore, conservation efforts are one of the effective ways  to ensure their survival.
Moreover, preventing extinction is not only about ethics but also about ecological stability and human well-being. For instance, bees are vital pollinators, and their disappearance would severely compromise agriculture and global food security. When it comes to human well-being, many species also contribute directly to medicine, tourism, and the economy. In medicine, biodiversity serves as a vast reservoir of potential treatments, meaning the loss of species could close the door on future scientific discoveries. Certain icon species have become a nation's symbol that draw millions of tourists annually, serving as a cultural and national asset. Because of that they can foster both pride and employment opportunities for humans. In this sense, preventing species from extinction is a prerequisite for human survival and progress.
In conclusion, while some extinctions in the distant past were unavoidable natural events, the present biodiversity crisis is overwhelmingly human-induced. For ethical, ecological, and economic reasons, I firmly believe that humans must take active responsibility in preventing further animal extinction.

As a result, art lessons can be seen as time-wasting to be compulsory in high school as it is less important and may impact on the student's performance in  academic examinations.

In addition, raising public awareness is also a great way to protect the Earth. When people are conscious about how harmful plastic is to the environment, they start to reduce the consumption of plastic bags, disposable goods and tend to choose eco-friendly items when shopping. In this sense, the influence of members of public to the environment is equal to politicians.
 
In conclusion, although authorities play the most decisive role in combating environmental challenges, I argue that the cooperation of ordinary people is equally necessary.

Living in a country where you have to speak a foreign language can cause serious social problems, as well as practical problems.
To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Some argue that being an expatriate and a non-native speaker can lead to several problems, regarding social and practical issues. While this notion is true to some extent, I am of the opinion that being exposed to foreign language can foster people’s bilingual skills, which is surprisingly vital in today’s world. 

It is understandable why some consider being a non-native speaker in foreign country can be detrimental for people’s social status as well as daily lives. Granted, language is the key of effective communication which means difficulties in language speaking can lead to misunderstanding in daily conversation with foreigners. When people struggle to express themselves, they might feel isolated or even excluded in a dialogue. Such language barriers can hinder one ability to establish relationships or engage fully in the social fabrics of a new environment. In terms of practical problems, underdeveloped language skills can make one’s daily life quite challenging. When people are not accustomed to one language, they might find daily activities that require language skills, such as using public transports or exchanging things frustrating due to the lack of language ability. 

However, this perspective somewhat overlooks the benefits of being exposed to foreign language to the expatriates. Living in a foreign country means people have to hear or use that language almost every day. By this repetition, people are likely to develop a language ability based on what they learn from native speakers, regarding pronunciation, intonation and so on. As a consequence, people living in foreign countries might adopt a second language, which can be seen as bilingual skill. Many researchers have pointed out that bilingual people have better flexibility in conversation and therefore, are more beneficial in their later life. 

In conclusion, non-native speakers are believed to be disadvantaged due to the challenges in social and practical life, from hindering social interactions to impeding daily tasks. However, those challenges are paled in comparison with the benefit of bilingual ability, which can be adopted through navigating a second language.

It is understandable why some consider being a non-native speaker in foreign country can be detrimental for people’s social status as well as daily lives. Such language barriers can hinder one ability to establish relationships or engage fully in the social fabrics of a new environment. Some individuals argue that team sports offer considerable benefits while others advocate for personal sports such as tennis or swimming. This essay will first closely examine both perspectives before showing my final thoughts.

It is justifiable that some appreciate team sports. First of all, individuals in a team can improve several skills such as communication, problem-solving and leadership through conflicts where all teammates are able to express their emotions. Moreover, each individual can obtain valuable techniques via cooperation with fellow members. Second, playing in a team not only enhances people’s physical health but also improves their mental health. This is mainly because collaborating with others alleviates feelings of isolation and develops a sense of community. Overall, this type of sport not only cultivates essential soft skills but also provides social support, which contributes significantly to participants’ overall well-being.

However, the benefits gained through practicing alone are undeniable. One major upside from this is being independent. Since no teammates are involved, it is essential for people to arrange personal practicing plans on their own according to their daily schedule, which encourages flexibility when participating in sports. As a result, they are likely to foster self-discipline as well as self-awareness in order to maintain efficiency when practicing. Additionally, there is a potential for people to develop greater concentration on themselves as well as better progression tracking. For instance, by recording the duration of each swimming lap, individuals can observe gradual improvements in their speed, helping them identify weakness and set particular goals.

In conclusion, while team sports offer certain advantages in terms of cooperation and mitigating isolation, individual exercises help people focus actively on personal developments. I argue that there should be a combination between both types so that people can not only acquire skills from others but also establish clear orientations for greater efficiency.

The issue of whether countries should aim for food self-sufficiency or rely partly on imports remains controversial. In my view, while reducing dependence on foreign supplies can bring certain benefits, it would be unrealistic and even counterproductive to insist that nations produce all their own food.
On the one hand, striving for greater food independence has undeniable advantages. Most importantly, it enhances national food security by protecting citizens from global supply chain disruptions, such as those witnessed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Furthermore, locally grown produce often ensures freshness and quality control compared to mass-imported goods. Supporting domestic farmers also stimulates rural economies and preserves agricultural traditions, thereby creating more resilient communities.
On the other hand, insisting on full self-sufficiency is neither feasible nor desirable. Climatic and geographical conditions mean that no single country can efficiently cultivate all types of food. For instance, tropical fruits cannot be produced in colder climates without exorbitant costs, leading to inefficient resource allocation. Moreover, international trade in food promotes comparative advantage , allowing nations to specialise in crops best suited to their environment while importing the rest at lower prices. This not only keeps food affordable but also fosters global cooperation and stability. Finally, diversity in diet, which is highly valued today, would be severely restricted if countries only consumed what they could produce domestically.
In conclusion, although a certain degree of domestic food production is essential for security, attempting to eliminate imports entirely would be impractical and economically damaging. A balanced approach—producing strategically important staples while importing complementary goods—appears to be the most sustainable path forward.

The issue of whether countries should aim for food self-sufficiency or rely partly on imports remains controversial. In my view, while reducing dependence on foreign supplies can bring certain benefits, it would be unrealistic and even counterproductive to insist that nations produce all their own food.
On the one hand, striving for greater food independence has undeniable advantages. Most importantly, it enhances national food security by protecting citizens from global supply chain disruptions, such as those witnessed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Furthermore, locally grown produce often ensures freshness and quality control compared to mass-imported goods. Supporting domestic farmers also stimulates rural economies and preserves agricultural traditions, thereby creating more resilient communities.
On the other hand, insisting on full self-sufficiency is neither feasible nor desirable. Climatic and geographical conditions mean that no single country can efficiently cultivate all types of food. For instance, tropical fruits cannot be produced in colder climates without exorbitant costs, leading to inefficient resource allocation. Moreover, international trade in food promotes comparative advantage , allowing nations to specialise in crops best suited to their environment while importing the rest at lower prices. This not only keeps food affordable but also fosters global cooperation and stability. Finally, diversity in diet, which is highly valued today, would be severely restricted if countries only consumed what they could produce domestically.
In conclusion, although a certain degree of domestic food production is essential for security, attempting to eliminate imports entirely would be impractical and economically damaging. A balanced approach—producing strategically important staples while importing complementary goods—appears to be the most sustainable path forward.
